Director of Supplier Quality
BAE Systems, Inc.
Fort Wayne, IN
Job Description
You don’t see it, but it’s there. Our employees work on the world’s most advanced electronics – from saving emissions in the City of Lights to powering the Mars Rover to protecting the F-35 fighter jet. At Electronic Systems, you’ll be among the brightest minds, working on the aerospace and defense industry’s most difficult problems. Drawing strength from our differences, we’re innovating for the future. And you can, too. We put our customers first – exemplified by our missions: “We Protect Those Who Protect Us®” and “We Innovate For Those Who Move The World®.” Sound like a team you want to be a part of?
Come build your career with BAE Systems at Fort Wayne, IN. Our flexible work environment provides you with a chance to change the world without giving up your personal life. Fort Wayne is centrally located between Indianapolis, Detroit, and Chicago for nearby cultural offerings and professional sports. It is the perfect size city; having enough selections of a big city yet small enough for convenience.

BAE Systems is seeking a Director of Supplier Quality, who will report to the Controls and Avionics Solutions (CAS) Senior Director of Quality and dotted line to the sector Senior Director of Supplier Quality. This role will be accountable for developing, maintaining, and optimizing Supplier Quality assurance strategy, reducing supplier quality risks and ensuring conforming products from the supply base. You will need to build strong relationships with the supply chain, operations, programs, and other quality functions to understand and translate requirements into a robust supplier quality executable plan that prevents disruptions and customer defects. In support of your supplier quality strategy, you will closely partner with the core teams of the sector supplier quality function to ensure the supply base is assessed, qualified, and consistently delivering a quality product. This will be a highly visible and key role to delivering value for the business. This individual must be a self-starting leader who can effectively partner with multiple functional organizations, internally, and suppliers, externally for success.
Key Responsibilities
Develop, communicate and drive a proactive Supplier Quality program for the business
Measure, maintain, analyze and communicate all Supplier Quality metrics, risks, and planned actions, and drive continuous improvements efforts at suppliers for improvement (CAR meetings, SRB, Mitigation meetings, etc.)
Partner with the Supplier Chain function to enforce contract/purchase order requirements, assess and develop suppliers, and drive robust RCCA with suppliers
Investigate, evaluate, and resolve supplier quality problems by analyzing defect trends, issuing SCARs, implementing improvement plans, conducting audits, and leading continuous improvement projects to drive a zero defects mindset
Responsible for developing a collaborative environment with suppliers, engineering, program quality, supplier chain, and operation leaders to resolve supplier issues
Engage/lead in all supply chain discussions to ensure proper selection of sourcing (throughout entire product life cycle) to mitigate risk and reduce overall cost of ownership of the parts
Partner with the sector Supplier Quality team to engage key supplier’s management in a business review process to monitor metrics, identify trends and implement programs to assure demonstrated performance improvements
Manages and develops a high performing team of Supplier Quality Engineers who can build relationships, interpret contractual and product requirements, and assist with flow down to suppliers
Owns and manages the Supplier Quality budget
Required travel of approximately 25%

Bachelor’s degree in technical field and 10+ years of experience or 14+ years of experience in lieu of degree
Experience in quality assurance/management within a regulated industry (aerospace, defense, medical), or the overall equivalent
Strong technical knowledge of quality science tools and methodologies, including statistical process control, APQP (PFMEA, Control Plans), and robust root cause analysis
Demonstrated success managing supplier improvements through audits and strong CAPA processes
Strong and demonstrated communication skills (written, verbal, visual) and interpersonal skills (listening and communicating within group working environment).
Organizational skills – can marshal resources to get things done, orchestrate multiple activities at once to accomplish a goal, use matrixed resources effectively and efficiently, and arrange information in a useful manner.

Engineering or Technical Bachelor's Degree
Master’s degree

Lean Six Sigma Greenbelt or Black Belt Certified

CIRCOR International, Inc.
Corona, CA
About CIRCOR Aerospace & Defense
CIRCOR Aerospace & Defense is focused on the design, development, and manufacture of specialty fluid and motion control products for demanding aerospace and defense applications. CIRCOR products are flying on most commercial and military aircraft, including single and twin aisle air transport, business and regional jets, military transports and fighters, and commercial and military rotorcraft. Other markets include unmanned aircraft, shipboard applications, and military ground vehicles.
Business units are in Corona, California; Warren, Massachusetts; Hauppauge, New York; Paris, France; Uxbridge, UK; and Tangier, Morocco. Parent company CIRCOR International is headquartered in Burlington, Massachusetts and CIRCOR Aerospace & Defense is headquartered in Corona, California.
POSITION DETAILS
Position Summary
As the Director of Quality, you will be responsible for leading quality initiatives that directly support our operational and site objectives. You will drive continuous improvement efforts focused on zero defect methodologies that aim to eliminate errors and defects in all production, office, engineering and service stages. The hands-on Quality leader is a leadership team member responsible for leading the organization. As a leadership team member, the successful candidate will partner with other staff members to execute the commitments of the business. Quality leadership includes recruiting, developing, training, coaching, goal and performance management. Shop floor processes producing close tolerance aerospace components produced via built to specification (BTS), build to print (BTP), maintenance repair and overhaul (MRO), supplemental type certification (STC), and Parts Manufacturing Approval (PMA). Typical processes include milling, lathe, hone, plating, CNC programming, assembly, testing, non-destructive testing, dimensional and visual inspection techniques, and electro-mechanical processes. Drive business metrics (safety, quality, on-time delivery, cost)
Zero Defect Plans
Driving systematic reduction of quality issues
Drive Prevention
Drive RCCA
Lead of Quality technical team
Interface with customers on key quality issues and initiatives
Own the QMS
Build and develop a high-performing quality team; provide hands-on coaching, establish performance standards, and foster a culture of accountability and continuous improvement
Lead quality system requirements, Build to Specifications, Build to Print, Repair Station
Lean / six sigma champion

Comply with all company policies/procedures.
Comply with all military and contractual requirements.
Perform additional related duties as assigned.

10 – 15 years of experience
Quality leadership, ability to mentor, coach, develop and build a high functioning quality team.
Quality systems experience, extensive understanding of quality systems and quality engineering focusing on lean manufacturing and lean processes in Build to Specifications, Build to Print, Repair Station, STC and PMA
High ethical standards. Models and supports organization’s goals and values; adapts to changing conditions; demonstrates persistence and overcomes obstacles.
Strong project management skills, including the ability to prioritize, balance, and manage multiple efforts with strong results/goal orientation. Use time effectively, prioritizes and organizes workflow; can orchestrate multiple activities at once. Agility and personal adaptability with the ability to successfully manage multiple priorities with a high sense of urgency in a rapidly changing environment.
Solid analytical skills and solution-driven thinking; collects and researches data; uses intuition and experience to complement data. Make good decisions based upon a mixture of analysis, wisdom, experience and judgment.
Identifies and resolves problems in a timely manner; develops alternative solutions; works well in group problem solving situations; presents ideas and information in a manner that gets others' attention; displays willingness to make decisions; exhibits sound and accurate judgment; supports and explains reasoning for decisions includes appropriate people in decision-making process.
Displays original thinking and creativity; Meets challenges with resourcefulness; Generates suggestions for improving work.
Learns quickly when facing new problems; a relentless and versatile learner; open to change; strives for continuous improvement of self and processes.
Enjoys working hard; action oriented and full of energy; enjoy challenges; drives for results. Versatility, flexibility and a willingness to work within constantly changing priorities with enthusiasm.
Excellent communication (oral and written) and interpersonal skills with the ability to convey information and ideas in a variety of media, tactful, confident, at all levels, internal and external.
Passion for data, analysis, trends, reporting and technology. Ability to read and interpret documents. Ability to write clearly and informatively routine reports, correspondence, and designs work flows and procedures. Presents numerical data effectively.
Advanced knowledge of JDE/MRP, Access, Word, Excel, Power Point, Visio, Project, and other applicable tools.
Ability to provide cross-functional and organizational leadership within a highly matrixed organization.
Demonstrated aptitude for process improvement and use of Lean and Six-Sigma resources and tools.
Demonstrated leadership skills including the ability to coach, assess, evaluate, develop, motivate and empower others.
Education & Experience
Bachelor of Science Degree in Engineering or related field, Master of Science in Engineering / Management or MBA preferred

Anduril Industries
Ashville, OH
Anduril Industries is a defense technology company with a mission to transform U.S. and allied military capabilities with advanced technology. Anduril’s family of systems is powered by Lattice OS, an AI-powered operating system that turns thousands of data streams into a realtime, 3D command and control center. Anduril, a leader in autonomous systems and weapons manufacturing, is building Arsenal-1, its first hyperscale manufacturing facility, just south of Columbus, Ohio in Pickaway County. Arsenal-1 is redefining the scale and speed that autonomous systems and weapons can be produced for the United States and its allies and partners. This is a monumental and essential step toward rebuilding America’s defense industrial base, strengthening America’s warfighting capabilities, and enhancing deterrence amid rising international threats.

The Connected Warfare will set the standard for building the future at Arsenal-1

our state-of-the-art manufacturing facility in Ashville, OH. This team will have the opportunity to train under our world-class manufacturing team at Anduril HQ in Costa Mesa, CA for 3 months before bringing that standard of excellence back to Ohio.
About The Role
As the Connected Warfare Deputy Head of Production, you will play a pivotal role in shaping the future of defense manufacturing by directly influencing the production of Anduril’s Connected Warfare product line. You will own the short-to-mid-term strategic development and execution of manufacturing operations, driving products to full-rate production. This role requires a dynamic leader who can serve as both a strategic architect and a hands-on executor, leading cross-functional teams to meet aggressive timelines and deliver products of the highest quality for our customers. You will contribute significantly to Anduril's vision of becoming a next-generation aerospace and defense manufacturer.
What You'll Do
Production Ownership & Strategy: Own all production outcomes for the Connected Warfare product line, including ramp plans, headcount, and the standing up of new manufacturing lines. Develop and execute a long-term strategy to rapidly scale production volumes to full-rate production.
Leadership & Team Management: Serve as a strategic leader and tactical do-er, driving all people and resources across production to achieve outcomes. Lead cross-functional teams (including Production, Supply Chain, Quality, and Manufacturing Engineering) through strong leadership, advocacy, and a consistent on-site presence, holding them accountable to meeting demands, deadlines, and goals.
Operational Excellence: Drive processes and systems needed throughout the product development lifecycle to mature products to full-rate production. Establish and manage the team to key performance indicators (KPIs) for financial, quality, and on-time delivery to optimize manufacturing operations' impact on the business.
Quality & Compliance: Be accountable to AS9100D guidelines and drive a "quality-first" culture across all manufacturing operations.
Process & Technology Advancement: Advise on development and oversee the implementation of digital technologies, from PLM and ERP to our custom MES and QMS systems, that enable our production operations to efficiently scale while meeting customer requirements. Shape corporate tools and processes to support the unique needs of aerospace production.
Required Qualifications
8+ years of proven experience overseeing the production and test of complex electromechanical products.
Strong leadership experience managing large (100+ person) manufacturing teams and directing large cross-functional teams across planning, supply chain, manufacturing engineering, quality, and production to deliver products of the highest quality.
A strong background in quality assurance, with a track record of driving a "quality-first" culture in a production environment and accountability to standards like AS9100D.
Past success operating in both low-rate prototype and high-rate manufacturing environments, with a proven ability to scale production.
High ownership and the ability to effectively manage multiple large projects and priorities in parallel, at a rapid pace, and report out on progress regularly.
Must be eligible to obtain and maintain a U.S. Secret security clearance.
Ability to work onsite five days a week at our Asheville, OH campus (Arsenal 1).
Preferred Qualifications
Success scaling production operations in a high-complexity manufacturing environment.
Deep experience with the niche supply chains for aerospace and robotics.
Demonstrated experience implementing and leveraging digital manufacturing technologies (PLM, ERP, MES, QMS) to drive efficiency and scale.

Anduril is committed to maintaining the integrity of our Talent acquisition process and the security of our candidates. evidence.text:
Director | Operational Excellence - Quality & Continuous Improvement
POLYWOOD®
Syracuse, IN
Director | Operational Excellence - Quality & Continuous Improvement
Syracuse, Indiana | On-Site | Full-Time
Help us build the way POLYWOOD® runs, improves, and grows.
At POLYWOOD®, we have built a strong business on hardworking people and the knowledge they bring to the job every day. As we grow, we have an opportunity to give our teams a common, structured way to solve problems, improve performance, and sustain the gains.
We are hiring a Director, Operational Excellence - Quality & Continuous Improvement to help us take that next step. This position partners directly with our COO to build and deploy THE POLYWOOD WAY, our management system and operating philosophy, across our manufacturing operations in Syracuse, Indiana, and Roxboro, North Carolina.
You will work alongside site and functional leaders to find the real root cause of problems, lead structured improvements in safety, quality, delivery, cost, and team performance, and build the routines that keep those improvements in place.
This is not a role for a scholar who teaches tools from a conference room. It is a hands-on opportunity for a practitioner who has led manufacturing teams, improved the areas they were responsible for, and enjoys helping others become better problem solvers.
Reporting directly to our Chief Operating Officer, you will have the opportunity to shape how POLYWOOD® manages, improves, and grows for years to come.
────────────────────────────────────────
The Work You Will Own
You will help turn THE POLYWOOD WAY into practical routines our teams use every day, from tiered management and daily huddles to standard work, visual management, and structured problem solving.
Your work will connect Quality, Lean, Continuous Improvement, data, and people development. You will put on your safety shoes and safety glasses, seek to understand the process first, and then help the people closest to the work make improvements that last.
────────────────────────────────────────
Where You Will Make an Impact
Partnering with the COO to develop, deploy, and continuously improve THE POLYWOOD WAY across both sites
Strengthening our tiered management system so goals on the floor line up with company goals for safety, quality, delivery, cost, and team
Leading setup reduction, value stream mapping, and root cause and countermeasure problem solving with the subject-matter experts who do the work
Leading quality strategy across both sites, including process controls, defect prevention, and corrective and preventive action
Applying structured problem solving beyond the plant floor, to challenges like team member turnover, warranty replacements, downtime, and training
Analyzing operational, quality, and cost data and turning findings into clear priorities for site and executive leaders
Validating the operational and financial results of improvements and building plans to sustain them
Building a network of Continuous Improvement resources and coaching supervisors and site leaders to solve problems on their own
Sharing effective practices between Syracuse and Roxboro and keeping standards consistent
────────────────────────────────────────
What You Bring
You have experience in manufacturing leadership, as a supervisor, manager, or plant manager, and you can speak to how you improved the area you were responsible for.
You have significant experience in manufacturing operations, Operational Excellence, Lean, Continuous Improvement, or Quality. You have personally led improvements, not only taught them, and you can explain tools like setup reduction, value stream mapping, and root cause problem solving in plain language.
You know that improvement starts with data you can trust, and when the data is noisy, you start by understanding the process gaps. You are comfortable influencing across functions and levels, including people who do not report to you.
Most importantly, you are hands-on, practical, and collaborative. You build the skills of others, follow through without unnecessary bureaucracy, and measure success by results that last.
Bonus Points
Experience with tiered management systems and strategic goal deployment
Experience leading improvements across more than one manufacturing site
Experience with Training Within Industry (TWI) or other structured training programs
Experience applying problem solving to turnover, hiring, or other business processes
Experience in extrusion, plastics, or building products manufacturing
────────────────────────────────────────
About Us
At POLYWOOD®, we design and build outdoor furniture that brings people together and stands the test of time. We do this using sustainable materials, including our genuine POLYWOOD® lumber made from recycled plastics. The strength of our products starts with the strength of our people.
Our manufacturing teams in Syracuse, Indiana, and Roxboro, North Carolina, build the products our customers love. THE POLYWOOD WAY will give those teams a common language and a structured way to keep getting better, together.
────────────────────────────────────────
What Makes This Role Special
You will help build something new.
You will shape THE POLYWOOD WAY and how it comes to life across both sites.
You will partner directly with the COO.
You will work closely with a leader who is passionate about building systems and developing people.
Your work will show up in real results.
Your improvements will be visible in safety, quality, delivery, cost, and team performance.
You will help people grow.
Many of our leaders have grown up within POLYWOOD®, and you will help them learn new ways of working that can change their careers.
You will join an “All Hands on the Rope” culture.
Improvement is everyone’s job here, from the leadership team to the shop floor.
You will be based in Syracuse with reach across both sites.
This position is on-site in Syracuse, Indiana, at least 80% of the time, with travel to Roxboro, North Carolina, as needed and up to 20% remote flexibility.
────────────────────────────────────────
If you are a hands-on leader who builds systems, develops people, and delivers results that last, we would love to hear from you.
────────────────────────────────────────
POLYWOOD is an equal opportunity employer. POLYWOOD evaluates qualified applicants without regard to characteristics protected by federal, state, or local laws.

Reporting to the Hub Director of Manufacturing, you will provide inspirational leadership in a rapidly growing business and have responsibility for all original equipment manufacturing at the site. This role demands a strategic, results-oriented leader with a proven track record of building and scaling rapidly growing organizations. Because of the need for consistent, in-person collaboration and/or the requirement to perform all work onsite due to the nature of this particular role, it will be performed full-time on site. Strategic Product Stream Leadership

  • Own the strategic direction, execution, and performance of the Circuit Card Assembly and Unit Integration factories
  • Serve as the primary point of contact between production and program management

Program Execution

  • Oversee execution of manufacturing in alignment with program schedules
  • Ensure all contractual obligations (cost, schedule, performance) are met or exceeded

Performance Improvement

  • Drive continuous improvement using Lean, Six Sigma Principles
  • Implement metrics to monitor production performance
  • Initiate corrective actions to resolve production variances, quality escapes, and manufacturing cost variances
Required Education, Experience, & Skills
  • Bachelors degree in Manufacturing, Industrial Technology, Operations Management, or related field; equivalent experience considered OR 20 years manufacturing experience with no degree
  • Minimum 10 years experience in production/manufacturing
  • Minimum 6 years experience leading production/manufacturing teams including managing people leaders
  • Proficiency with manufacturing management concepts
  • Proficiency applying Lean Manufacturing principles and visual management tools
Preferred Education, Experience, & Skills
  • Proficiency with Oracle ERP
  • Formal Lean or Six Sigma training/certification
  • Minimum 10 years experience leading people leaders of production/manufacturing teams

Full-Time Salary Range: $153377 - $260743

Sr. Manager of Adventure Products
Rivian
Irvine, CA
About Rivian
Rivian is on a mission to keep the world adventurous forever. This goes for the emissions-free Electric Adventure Vehicles we build, and the curious, courageous souls we seek to attract.
As a company, we constantly challenge what's possible, never simply accepting what has always been done. We reframe old problems, seek new solutions and operate comfortably in areas that are unknown. Our backgrounds are diverse, but our team shares a love of the outdoors and a desire to protect it for future generations.
Role Summary
As the Senior Manager of Adventure Products, you will lead our Industrial Design Product Team focused on expanding the Rivian experience beyond the vehicle itself. Reporting directly to the Senior Director of Exterior Design, you will oversee the end-to-end design strategy and execution across vehicle accessories, off-the-shelf brand partnerships, gear, apparel, lifestyle merchandise, and toys.
This role requires a proven design leader with extensive hands-on production experience and deep factory-level relationships. You will bridge high-level visionary product strategy with rigorous manufacturing execution, ensuring every product meets Rivian's world-class design standards while scaling effectively into mass production.
Responsibilities
Design Leadership & Team Management
Lead, mentor, and inspire a high-performing team of industrial designers focused on vehicle accessories, hardgoods, softgoods, lifestyle gear, and toys.
Expand the aesthetic, functional, and strategic design vision for all non-vehicle physical products, maintaining alignment with Rivian's core vehicle design language.
Manage project workflows, design reviews, timelines, and resource allocation across multiple concurrent product programs.
Product Strategy & Range Execution
Vehicle Accessories:
Drive design innovation for internal and customer-facing vehicle accessories (e. g. , gear tunnel components, roof racks, camping gear, cargo management, lighting, and overland equipment).
Toy & Merch Strategy:
Build and execute a cohesive brand merchandise and toy strategy that engages enthusiasts, children, and Rivian owners worldwide.
Off-the-Shelf & Licensing Partnerships:
Evaluate, curate, and direct third-party supplier products and collaborative brand partnerships, ensuring off-the-shelf items are elevated to meet Rivian's premium design standards.
Production, Manufacturing & Factory Engagement
Leverages extensive production experience and direct factory contacts to push concepts through DFM (Design for Manufacturing) into successful mass production.
Work directly on factory floors-both domestically and internationally-to troubleshoot prototyping, tooling, material selection, CMF (Color, Material, Finish), and production challenges.
Collaborate closely with Purchasing, Supply Chain, Hardware Engineering, and Quality teams to ensure design intent, cost targets, and launch schedules are strictly maintained.
Qualifications
To Apply:
Please include a direct link to your portfolio (and any access credentials if password-protected), featuring work in industrial design, softgoods/hardgoods, and production-ready physical products. Experience:
10+ years of professional industrial design experience, with at least 3-5+ years in a team management or leadership capacity.
Production Mastery:
Demonstrated track record of bringing complex physical products from concept through high-volume mass production.
Factory Network & Technical Expertise:
Must-have
established direct relationships and hands-on experience working directly with factories, suppliers, and overseas/domestic manufacturing partners. Proven capability to push factory partners to achieve tight design tolerances and premium finishing.
Category Diversity:
Prior background designing across diverse categories-such as outdoor/adventure gear, automotive accessories, consumer electronics, hardgoods, toys, or technical softgoods-is highly preferred.
Design Excellence:
Exceptional portfolio demonstrating strong ID fundamentals, form development, sketching, 3D CAD modeling, CMF mastery, and user-centered design thinking.
Cross-Functional Collaboration:
Strong ability to communicate design vision and negotiate technical/budget constraints with engineering, supply chain, and executive stakeholders.
Travel:
Ability to travel domestically and internationally (up to 20-30%) to visit factory partners, suppliers, and testing environments.
Bonus Qualifications
Passion for the outdoors, electric vehicles, overland travel, and adventure culture.
Background in developing both hardgoods (tooling, injection molding, metal fabrication)
and softgoods/textiles.
Pay Disclosure
The salary range for this role is $196,000 - $259,700 for California based applicants. This is the lowest to highest salary we in good faith believe we would pay for this role at the time of this posting. An employee's position within the salary range will be based on several factors including, but not limited to, specific competencies, relevant education, qualifications, certifications, experience, skills, geographic location, shift, and organizational needs.
The successful candidate may be eligible for annual performance bonus and equity awards.
We offer a comprehensive package of benefits for full-time and part-time employees, their spouse or domestic.

Ensure a healthy and safe working environment while complying with federal and state regulations through active collaboration with environmental, health, and safety (EHS) staff

Ability to influence others via communication to get desired results

Excellent customer-relations skills
